reichstag: Reichstag, Brandenburg Gate and Holocaust Memorial

The German Parliament with Norman Foster's glass dome, a short walk from the Brandenburg Gate, the symbol of the city: from the square you can also walk to the Memorial to the Murdered Jews of Europe, the field of 2,711 concrete slabs.
linden: Unter den Linden, Gendarmenmarkt and Humboldt Forum

The great avenue of the historic centre: Opernplatz with the State Opera, the Neue Wache, the French and German Cathedrals on either side of the Gendarmenmarkt (Berlin's most beautiful square), up to the rebuilt palace that houses the Humboldt Forum.
museum: The island on the Spree with five UNESCO-listed museums. The favourite is the Neues Museum with the famous bust of Nefertiti; nearby, on the Lustgarten, stands Berlin Cathedral with its panoramic dome.
fernseh: East Germany's 368-metre television tower, visible from almost everywhere: from the platform at 203 metres there's a 360-degree view of all Berlin. At its foot is Alexanderplatz, the heart of former East Berlin, with the World Clock.
mauer: The best-preserved stretch of the border: the death strip with a section of original wall, the Chapel of Reconciliation and open-air exhibitions with photos of residents escaping through their windows. The documentation centre's tower lets you look down on the "strip".
eastside: 1.3 kilometres of original Wall repainted in 1990 by artists from all over the world: the mural of the kiss between Brezhnev and Honecker is the most famous. It ends at the Oberbaumbrücke, the red-brick bridge over the Spree.
potsdamer: Topography of Terror and Potsdamer Platz

A free indoor and outdoor museum built where the Gestapo and SS headquarters stood, next to a stretch of original Wall; nearby is Potsdamer Platz, the modern district built on the gap left by the Wall, and the very touristy Checkpoint Charlie.
kreuz: Berlin's most varied neighbourhood, with murals, Turkish shops and alternative bars: Markthalle Neun is a 19th-century covered market with producers and street food, and Oranienstraße is the heart of the nightlife.
prenz: The neighbourhood of Art Nouveau buildings and cafés, with the Mauerpark: a park that used to be the border strip, with a stretch of Wall and, on Sundays, a flea market and open-air karaoke.
tiergarten: The great park in the centre, with wide tree-lined avenues, the Neuer See lake and the golden Victory Column on its roundabout. You can climb the Column for the view down the avenues.
